_comment: R-104. Branch protection lives in GitHub settings, not in the checkout, so
from the repository alone every gate in ci.yml is advisory: nothing here
could prove that a red conformance run stops a merge.
This file is the project's CLAIM about which ci.yml jobs must be required
status checks on the protected branch. Two things check it:
'required-checks' workflow, asks the GitHub API for the branch's
ACTUAL required checks and fails if any name below is missing;
* tests/required-checks-manifest.test.ts keeps the claim honest without
any network: every `job` must exist in ci.yml, every `check` must match
that job's display name, and every job in ci.yml must appear in exactly
`check` is the name GitHub shows (a job's `name:` if it has one, otherwise
its id) — that string, not the job id, is what branch protection matches.
Moving an entry into `not_required` is a deliberate decision and needs a
reason. Deleting one is not a way to make the checker pass.

required.check: Lint — no silent test skips, no active TODO markers
Lint — SDK envelope fixture drift + interop coverage
Lint — SDK BIP-143 fixture drift + interop coverage

not_required.reason: Guarded by `if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.run_teranode`, so it does not run on a pull request at all. A required check that never reports blocks every merge forever, which is why an opt-in job must stay out of the list.
